You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-c8b5b712: fill hollow rectangular outlines by interior parity

Use when this task recurs with a fresh ARC grid containing hollow, one-cell-thick rectangular outlines in different colors, on a uniform background.

## Transformation

For each fully enclosed rectangular outline, keep its perimeter unchanged and fill every cell strictly inside the perimeter:

- Fill with color **2** when both interior height and interior width are even.
- Otherwise fill with color **7**.

Thus the 2/7 choice depends on whether *both* strict-interior dimensions are even, not on outline color, area, or size alone. Compute strict-interior dimensions as `(outer_height - 2, outer_width - 2)`. Leave unrelated cells and all outline cells unchanged. Handle each outline independently, including multiple separate outlines with the same perimeter color.

## Evidence

Two demos supported this rule. Outlines with strict interiors 1x1, 2x3, 3x3, and 5x5 received fill 7. Outlines with strict interiors 2x2 and 4x4 received fill 2. The test instance had a 5x5 outline (3x3 interior) and multiple 3x3 outlines (1x1 interiors); each interior received 7. Submitting 2 in the 3x3 interior of the 5x5 outline was incorrect; changing that interior to 7, while keeping the others 7, solved that instance. A separate solved recurrence contained a 4x4 outline with a 2x2 interior filled 2 and a 5x5 outline with a 3x3 interior filled 7, further confirming the parity rule across different outline colors.

## Additional confirmed recurrence

A 13x15 test contained three hollow square outlines: a 3x3 color-0 outline (strict interior 1x1), a 7x7 color-6 outline (strict interior 5x5), and a 3x3 color-8 outline (strict interior 1x1). All three interiors were filled with 7 and the instance was accepted. This also confirms that outline colors may vary within one grid and that the rule applies independently to each enclosed outline. In one attempted response, a row with only 14 entries made the grid invalid; validate every output row has the original width.

A further accepted 16x9 recurrence had a 7x7 color-1 outline at rows 0–6, columns 0–6, and a 7x7 color-3 outline at rows 8–14, columns 1–7; both strict interiors were 5x5 and were filled with 7. The other cells, including the color-8 background and gap, remained unchanged. This confirms the rule on two same-sized but differently colored outlines in one test.

## Additional accepted recurrence

A 13x28 test had five outlines of differing colors and sizes. A 3x3 color-6 outline (1x1 interior) and a 3x3 color-4 outline (1x1 interior) were filled with 7. A 6x6 color-3 outline (4x4 interior), a 4x4 color-5 outline (2x2 interior), and a 6x6 color-1 outline (4x4 interior) were filled with 2. The instance was accepted. This further confirms the condition is exactly that both strict-interior dimensions are even, independent of outline color or whether the outline is square.

## Additional accepted recurrence

A 22x17 test had an 8x8 color-6 outline (strict interior 6x6) and a 3x3 color-3 outline (strict interior 1x1), plus a separate 3x3 color-0 object with one center cell missing. The 6x6 rectangle interior was filled with 2, the 1x1 interior with 7, and the separate color-0 shape's center with 7; all frames, background cells, and other pixels were preserved. This recurrence confirms the interior-parity rule also applies when a distinct non-rectangular/partially hollow object is nearby: only the closed rectangular outlines are treated as frames, while the separate object remains unchanged.

## Additional accepted recurrence

A 20x29 test contained three hollow frames on background 1: color-5 outer 4x4 at rows 0–3, cols 4–7 (strict interior 2x2) filled 2; color-4 outer 7x7 at rows 6–12, cols 13–19 (strict interior 5x5) filled 7; and color-5 outer 3x3 at rows 14–16, cols 10–12 (strict interior 1x1) filled 7. The instance was accepted. This confirms mixed frame colors/sizes and independent application within one grid.

## Additional accepted recurrence

A 12x14 test on background 1 contained three 3x3 hollow frames, each with a 1x1 strict interior: color 8 at rows 4–6, columns 7–9; color 5 at rows 6–8, columns 0–2; and color 3 at rows 8–10, columns 10–12. Each center was filled with 7 and the instance was accepted. This further confirms 1x1 interiors receive 7 across multiple frame colors and positions in one grid.

## Application checklist

1. Find each complete rectangular perimeter of a single non-background color; distinguish nearby separate outlines.
2. Compute strict interior dimensions: outer height minus 2, outer width minus 2.
3. Fill only the strict interior with 2 iff both dimensions are even; otherwise use 7.
4. Preserve dimensions, perimeter pixels, exterior/background cells, and unrelated objects. Validate row widths and ensure no perimeter pixels were overwritten.

## Caution

Do not assign the fill color based on the perimeter color. The demonstrations include identical perimeter colors with differing fill colors, and different perimeter colors with identical fill colors.
